name: test-2-greatest-percentage-decline
question: Which store experienced the greatest percentage revenue decline?
answer_text:
smart_toy

Scope: 2025 → 2029 (first and last years in the data); physical stores only (the website is a separate channel; excluded unless asked); all categories; all Market tiers.

Findings

20 of 20 stores compared declined between 2025 and 2029.
Largest decline: SH11 – Chicago, IL (4-Large): $539,740.00 in 2025 → $179,130.00 in 2029 (-66.81%). Within 4-Large it ranks 1 of 3 (1 = largest decline); the 4-Large median change was -47.27%, so it is 19.54 points below its tier's median.
Next largest declines: SH13 – Denver, CO (3-Medium) -49.43%; SH06 – Columbus, OH (2-Minor) -48.99%.
Median change by Market tier: 1-Small -48.58% (6 stores); 2-Minor -48.06% (6 stores); 3-Medium -48.45% (5 stores); 4-Large -47.27% (3 stores).

Interpretation

Every store compared declined, so the question is how much, not whether.
Revenue is not profit: costs are not in the data.
Compares 2025 with 2029 only; the years in between are not used.
Stores differ in size (Market tier), so compare percentage change, and compare a store with others in the same tier (its rank within the tier and the tier medians).
The website (SH00) is excluded by default because it is a different sales channel; choose the Website channel to include it.
A change in revenue does not explain why it changed; the reasons are not in the data.

Next steps

name: test-4-satisfaction-causes-revenue
question: Does higher customer satisfaction cause higher revenue?
answer_text:
smart_toy

Scope: all years; all Market tiers; physical stores with a survey score.

Findings

Correlation between satisfaction and revenue across 100 store-years: +0.235 (weak).
1-Small: correlation -0.01 (n = 30); mean satisfaction 3.54, mean store-year revenue $72,964.67.
2-Minor: correlation -0.09 (n = 30); mean satisfaction 3.06, mean store-year revenue $96,821.00.
3-Medium: correlation -0.01 (n = 25); mean satisfaction 3.12, mean store-year revenue $145,690.00.
4-Large: correlation +0.18 (n = 15); mean satisfaction 4.28, mean store-year revenue $414,649.33.

Interpretation

Based on 100 store-years (one survey score each).
Overall (all tiers together) the correlation is weak (+0.235, n = 100).
Within Market tiers, the correlation is near zero in 1-Small (-0.01, n = 30), 2-Minor (-0.09, n = 30), and 3-Medium (-0.01, n = 25); weak in 4-Large (+0.18, n = 15, a small sample).
Strength labels: |r| below 0.1 near zero, below 0.3 weak, below 0.5 moderate, otherwise strong; fewer than 20 store-years is a small sample.
This is an association, not causation: a correlation cannot show that satisfaction causes revenue (or that revenue causes satisfaction).
Market tier confounds the comparison: larger stores earn more whatever their satisfaction, so compare the within-tier correlations.
The survey reflects active customers only; people who stopped shopping at a store are not surveyed.
Revenue is not profit: costs are not in the data.
5 Website store-year(s) were excluded: there is no in-store survey for the website, so their satisfaction is blank.

Next steps

No recommendation is supported by this data.
Showing that satisfaction drives revenue would need more than this data, e.g. a planned service change at some stores compared with others.
